story: A website took Rs 15,500 for a smartwatch on 18 October 2026 and then disappeared. Can I get an FIR registered under Section 154 CrPC? I live in Bhubaneswar.

timeline.event: Paid Rs 15,500 for a smartwatch on a website
timeline.user_words: A website took Rs 15,500 for a smartwatch on 18 October 2026

facts.user_goal: Get an FIR registered under Section 154 CrPC

rules.name: consumer_limitation
rules.message: File your consumer complaint before 18 Oct 2028 (710 days left). This counts 2 years from 18 Oct 2026 (your purchase date - counted from the earliest possible day, to be safe). Don't wait for the last date. Sending a letter or calling the helpline does NOT pause this clock.

facts_used.start_basis: purchase date (earliest possible start, to be safe)

rules.label: Last date to file your consumer complaint

rules.name: forum_and_fee
rules.message: You paid Rs 15,500, so the complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission, with no filing fee. You can file in the district where you live or work, online at e-jagriti.gov.in. You don't need a lawyer to file.
rules.label: Where to file

rules.name: free_first_steps
rules.message: Two free steps often work first: (1) a written complaint to the seller's or platform's grievance officer, (2) the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
rules.label: Try these first

answer.summary: You can file a consumer complaint for your Rs 15,500 smartwatch refund. The website's disappearance after taking your money is an unfair trade practice and a deficiency. You have about 710 days left to file. You do not need a lawyer. You can file online at e-jagriti.gov.in. An FIR is for the police to investigate a crime, which is a separate process from getting your money back.

claims.text: You are a consumer because you bought a smartwatch for personal use and paid Rs 15,500.
The website taking your money and disappearing is an unfair trade practice because it is refusing to refund your money.
You can file a consumer complaint with the District Commission in Bhubaneswar. There is no filing fee because you paid up to Rs 5 lakh.
You must file your complaint within two years of 18 October 2026.

next_steps.action: Call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.

next_steps.why: This is a free first step to try to get your money back before filing a formal complaint.

next_steps.why: You can file in the district where you live. There is no fee.

support.text: You are a consumer because you bought a smartwatch for personal use and paid Rs 15,500.
support.reason: The law text defines 'consumer' as any person who buys any goods for consideration, which is paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised, or under any system of deferred payment. The sentence states the person bought a smartwatch for personal use and paid Rs 15,500, which fits the definition of buying goods for consideration paid. The personal use aspect is consistent with 'consumer' as the exclusion is only for resale or commercial purpose.

support.text: The website taking your money and disappearing is an unfair trade practice because it is refusing to refund your money.
support.reason: The law text explicitly includes 'refusing, after selling goods or rendering services, to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration thereof, if paid' as an unfair trade practice. The sentence states the website is refusing to refund money, which directly matches this provision.

support.text: You can file a consumer complaint with the District Commission in Bhubaneswar. There is no filing fee because you paid up to Rs 5 lakh.
support.reason: The law text states 'District Commission: consideration paid up to Rs 50 lakh' for pecuniary jurisdiction. The sentence mentions filing with District Commission for up to Rs 5 lakh, which falls within this limit. The 'no filing fee' claim is not addressed in this law text, but the question asks only about the legal rule regarding which commission can hear the complaint, and that is supported.

support.text: You can file a consumer complaint with the District Commission in Bhubaneswar. There is no filing fee because you paid up to Rs 5 lakh.
support.reason: The law text explicitly states 'No fee where the consideration paid is up to Rs 5 lakh.' The sentence states there is no filing fee because paid up to Rs 5 lakh, which directly matches.

support.text: You can file a consumer complaint with the District Commission in Bhubaneswar. There is no filing fee because you paid up to Rs 5 lakh.
support.reason: The law text provides that a complaint may be instituted in a District Commission where 'the complainant resides or personally works for gain' (clause d). The sentence states the complainant can file with District Commission in Bhubaneswar. Whether this is correct depends on the complainant's residence, but the legal rule permitting filing in the complainant's District Commission is present in the law text.

support.text: You can file a consumer complaint with the District Commission in Bhubaneswar. There is no filing fee because you paid up to Rs 5 lakh.
support.reason: The law text states a complaint may be filed with a District Commission by 'the consumer' to whom goods are sold or delivered. The sentence states the person can file a consumer complaint. The 'no filing fee' part is not addressed in this law text, but the legal rule about who may file is supported.

support.text: You must file your complaint within two years of 18 October 2026.
support.reason: The law text states complaints must be filed within 'two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen.' The sentence specifies 'two years of 18 October 2026' - a specific date rather than 'from the date on which the cause of action has arisen.' The law requires the period to be calculated from the cause of action date, not from a fixed calendar date. This adds a condition (fixed date) not present in the law text.

draft:
Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: [FILL: name of the other party], [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for refund

On 18 October 2026 I paid Rs 15,500 to you for [FILL: product/service and order number]. [FILL: what went wrong, e.g. product defective / service not provided]. Despite my requests you have not refunded the amount.

I request a full refund of Rs 15,500 within 15 days of receiving this letter.

If the refund is not made, I intend to file a complaint before the District Consumer Commission under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: [FILL: receipts, chats, emails, bank statements].

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in the invoice, order page, or the seller's 'grievance officer' details on the website/app.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.69 (Two-year limitation and condonation); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.34(2) (Where to file: District Commission); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.35(1) (Who may file a complaint; e-filing)
